item.title: Payments, Privacy and Travel Conditions Shift
item.description: Payment rules, privacy enforcement, travel conditions and market access changed in concrete ways.
item.content:encoded:
Payment rules, privacy enforcement, travel conditions and market access changed in concrete ways.

  1. Australia’s card-surcharge ban starts 1 October Visa, Mastercard, American Express and eftpos card networks will prohibit card surcharges in Australia from 1 October, covering in-store and online card payments. 21 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up
  2. Vietnam floods inundate more than 16,000 homes Flooding across northern and central Vietnam has inundated more than 16,000 homes and left roads and low-lying areas submerged, materially disrupting travel in affected provinces. 19 Sep 2026. AP · Follow up
  3. Bank of Japan raises rate to 1.25% The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate from 1.00% to 1.25%, its highest level since 1995. 21 Sep 2026. News.com.au · Follow up
  4. Google fined €403 million over location-data processing Ireland’s Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million after an inquiry into its processing of location data. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  5. US SEC opens five-year path for tokenized stocks The US Securities and Exchange Commission created a five-year exemption for qualifying tokenized-stock trading while requiring the tokens to carry the same shareholder rights as the underlying shares. 17 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  6. Wellington approves second central-city bus corridor Wellington City Council approved the Harbour Quays bus-priority project, with a new two-way waterfront bus corridor, new or upgraded stops and implementation work expected to begin in 2027. 17 Sep 2026. Metlink · Follow up
  7. Pixel September update adds faster VIP contacts Google began rolling out the September Pixel Drop to Pixel 6 and newer phones, adding one-tap VIP contact actions and notification badges; Pixel Watch 3 and newer also gain expanded one-handed notification gestures. 15 Sep 2026. Android Authority · Follow up
  8. Android adds remembered-item tracking without a tag Google’s September Android Drop lets supported Android 16+ devices save where untagged items such as passports or spare keys were placed in Find Hub, with optional photos. 1 Sep 2026. Google · Follow up
  9. Fabric SQL editor upgrades reach general availability Microsoft Fabric’s September release moved SQL query-editor enhancements to general availability, including a faster results grid, scalable object explorer, IntelliSense, autosave controls and SQL file import/export. Sep 2026. Microsoft Learn · Follow up
  10. Gemini 3.8 Live models launch for real-time voice Google launched Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking for real-time voice-agent workloads, with the new models also feeding voice capabilities across Google products. 16 Sep 2026. Times of India · Follow up
  11. Australian wholesale power prices fall sharply Wholesale electricity prices in Australia fell 21% to 43% year-on-year across states in the September quarter, reducing the wholesale component feeding future retail electricity costs. 21 Sep 2026. The Australian · Follow up
  12. China slows humanoid-robot IPO pipeline Chinese regulators have used informal guidance to slow some humanoid-robot listings after volatile trading in the sector, tightening the near-term pipeline for a heavily funded investment theme. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  13. Trafigura launches 14-tanker Volare unit Trafigura launched Volare Shipping with six operating supertankers and eight more on order, and plans a private placement followed by an Oslo listing around 5 October. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  14. Yuan reaches strongest level since January 2023 China’s onshore yuan strengthened to 6.6957 per US dollar, its strongest level in more than three and a half years. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters via MarketScreener · Follow up
  15. Typhoon Dujuan disrupts travel in eastern Japan Typhoon Dujuan brought heavy rain and landslide warnings to eastern Japan, including the Kanto region, and disrupted scheduled events and travel movements. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  16. Fed and BoE probe bank exposure after Jane Street loss The US Federal Reserve and Bank of England are collecting information on banks’ exposure and risk controls around major trading firms after Jane Street sustained a reported $15 billion loss. 21 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  17. Four Chinese companies launch Hong Kong offerings Four Chinese companies launched or prepared Hong Kong share offerings seeking up to HK$14.35 billion in total, with trading scheduled to begin on 29 September. 20 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  18. AFL final drives exceptional Melbourne airfares Return economy fares from Perth and Brisbane to Melbourne surged into the thousands of Australian dollars for grand-final week even after airlines added thousands of extra seats. 21 Sep 2026. The Australian · Follow up

item.title: Rules, Routes and Digital Risks Shift
item.description: Building rules, travel capacity, security fixes and practical digital tools changed in concrete ways.
item.content:encoded:
Building rules, travel capacity, security fixes and practical digital tools changed in concrete ways.

  1. NZ earthquake rules remove nearly 3,000 buildings Parliament passed reforms that will remove about 2,900 buildings from the earthquake-prone register; most remaining reforms start 1 July 2027. 19 Sep 2026. 1News · Follow up
  2. NZ clinical-trial contractor confirms health-data theft Dunedin contractor ZenTech confirmed health and identifying clinical-trial data was stolen; reporting says about 67GB was exfiltrated while Health NZ said its own systems were not breached. 19 Sep 2026. MedRisk · Follow up
  3. Pixel modem zero-click flaw is actively exploited Google's September Pixel patch fixes CVE-2026-58704, a cellular-modem authorization flaw Google says saw limited targeted exploitation; CISA added it to its exploited-vulnerability list. 16 Sep 2026. Android Authority · Follow up
  4. Air New Zealand expands Auckland–Hobart season The seasonal route returns 25 October and will run through April 2027 with up to 170 flights and more than 33,000 seats, 28% more capacity than last season. 19 Sep 2026. Aviation A2Z · Follow up
  5. Nine more NZ hotels receive Michelin keys Michelin added nine New Zealand properties to its 2026 hotel selection and promoted three properties to two-key status, bringing the national total to 28 key hotels. 19 Sep 2026. 1News · Follow up
  6. Power BI gains Fabric Real-Time Hub subscriptions Power BI semantic models can now subscribe directly to Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Hub event streams for sub-minute dashboard updates on supported Premium Per User and Fabric capacities. 18 Sep 2026. Akshara Technologies · Follow up
  7. Claude adds native Docs and Slides tools Anthropic began rolling out a unified Claude interface plus Docs and Slides, letting Pro and Max users create and export documents and presentations directly from Claude. 16 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  8. Marvel's Wolverine is now available on PS5 Insomniac's AAA Marvel's Wolverine launched on 15 September; current critic aggregates are generally favorable and PlayStation Store player ratings reported after launch are strongly positive. 15 Sep 2026. GeekBlog · Follow up
  9. Australia opens consultation on frontier-AI and data-centre standards The federal government opened consultation on new national standards for data centres and frontier-AI training while also considering restrictions on smart glasses in Commonwealth workplaces. 17 Sep 2026. ABC · Follow up
  10. Anthropic commits to first Australian data centre Anthropic agreed to lease land for a large AI-inference data centre in western Queensland as part of the planned Western Downs Digital Park, with the first stage slated to open in 2027. 16 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up
  11. Australia moves toward algorithm-choice rights Australia's government is advancing plans that would let social-media users control or opt out of algorithmically selected content, extending its online-platform rules beyond the under-16 account restrictions. 19 Sep 2026. Guardian · Follow up
  12. Russian ESPO crude trades above US$120 Reuters calculations and trader data put Russia's ESPO Blend above US$120 a barrel in mid-September, with premiums over Brent reaching record levels as Chinese refiners bought more cargoes. 18 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  13. China keeps benchmark lending rates unchanged China left its one-year Loan Prime Rate at 3.00% and five-year rate at 3.50% for a 16th month, fixing the September benchmark used across loans and mortgages. 20 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  14. Australian refinance market now has 50 sub-6% lenders Fifty Australian lenders are offering variable home-loan rates below 6%, up from 38 in June; the lowest cited refinance rate is 5.69% for borrowers meeting its equity requirement. 17 Sep 2026. The Australian · Follow up
  15. Rocket Lab launches 12th StriX radar satellite from NZ Rocket Lab's Electron launched from Mahia and placed Synspective's 12th StriX synthetic-aperture-radar satellite into a 572km orbit, the company's 17th launch of 2026. 19 Sep 2026. Space.com · Follow up
  16. China's CXMT starts mass production of new DRAM platform CXMT said its fifth-generation DRAM platform entered mass production and introduced 24-gigabit LPDDR5X chips, increasing memory density for phones and portable devices. 20 Sep 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  17. Qwen releases new multimodal Omni Flash model Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash was released on 18 September, adding a new multimodal model option to the rapidly expanding set of current open and frontier AI tools. 18 Sep 2026. LLM Releases · Follow up
  18. Wellington's Non Disclosed Artist exhibition opens this week A new exhibition bringing together 28 artists and creatives from Wellington's film, games and wider creative community opens at Thistle Hall on 21 September and runs 22–27 September. 20 Sep 2026. Thistle Hall · Follow up
